newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Schroders upgrades Portugal's BCP rating.
newsitem.headline: Schroders upgrades Portugal's BCP rating.

text.p: Schroders Securities said it had upgraded the rating of Banco Comercial Portugues from 'perform in line' to 'outperform' in a report dated June 16.
BCP's share price at that date was 3,450 escudos; today shares were trading at 3,350 escudos.
The Schroders report said that BCP shares were at a premium of eight percent to the banking sector average, but seven percent below the sector average in Spain.
"In terms of valuation, BCP is negotiating with a price/earnings ratio of 15.4 for 1998 results, a premium eight percent above the sector average," the report said.
Schroders said: "BCP's growth, quality and size justify this premium".

The report added that concerns about an eventual share capital increase had diminished, and that the acquisition of more than 25 percent of Banco Portugues do Atlantico from Imperio would have a positive impact on results.
Schroders said it forecast that BCP would end financial year 1997 with net profits of 28.054 billion escudos, rising to 33.538 billion and 38.315 billion in 1998 and 1999 respectively.
Expected Earnings Per Share (EPS) in 1997 is 187 escudos, which should rise to 224 and 255 escudos in 1998 and 1999 respectively.
